title: The Rise of Artifact Evaluation in Systems Research (2011-2019)
explainer: Reproducing a systems or architecture paper used to mean reading the PDF and hoping the described experiment matched reality. The practice of formally checking this was introduced as 'artifact evaluation' by the software engineering community at ESEC/FSE in 2011, and systems venues followed only years later — ACM SIGOPS's flagship conference, SOSP, had adopted its own artifact-evaluation track by 2019. Those evaluations award badges for whether code is publicly available, functional, and whether a paper's results can actually be independently reproduced, which is exactly the skill this lesson asks you to practice by hand.
